literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 诺如病毒感染的总体患病率为44%,其中GII型(73%)占主导地位,GI型占18%。9%的病例检测到GI/GII共感染。年龄与诺如病毒基因型分布存在显著关联(p=0.03),且GII型在≤5岁儿童中更为普遍。 [10.5897/jgmv2026.0086]
与 DMSO 处理的对照相比,TAK-779 在感染后 48 小时和 96 小时 (hpi) 时,GII.17 HuNoV 复制分别增加了 2.3 倍和 6.0 倍。 [10.1111/gtc.70139]
诺如病毒 在整个研究期间均被检测到,其中 3 月份的月度比例最高(34.4%)。高原州立专科医院阳性病例比例最大(68.9%),各机构差异有统计学意义。 [10.9734/sajrm/2026/v20i9523]

轮状病毒 A 患病率 为 2.5%。患病率 最高的病原体是肠聚集性大肠杆菌 (EAEC) (52.6%,20/38)、志贺氏菌/肠侵袭性大肠杆菌 (Shigella/EIEC (76.3%,29/38)、诺如病毒 (26.3%,10/38),贾第鞭毛虫是鉴定的主要寄生虫。合并感染率较高(94.7%,36/38),大多数严重病例(75%,3/4)中存在细菌-病毒合并感染(73.3%,11/15)。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0356904]
给予最低剂量的酵母聚糖佐剂的 VLP 疫苗 的婴儿小鼠表现出肠道和唾液 VLP 特异性 IgA 抗体以及血浆 VLP 特异性 IgG 抗体水平的增加,与成人相当。相比之下,仅接受 VLP 的幼年小鼠的 免疫应答 明显较弱。 [10.1016/j.mucimm.2026.100401]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The overall prevalence of norovirus infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. A significant association was observed between age and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. [10.5897/jgmv2026.0086]
TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. [10.1111/gtc.70139]

Norovirus was detected throughout the study period, with the highest monthly proportion recorded in March (34.4%). Plateau State Specialist Hospital accounted for the largest proportion of positive cases (68.9%), and the difference by facility was statistically significant. [10.9734/sajrm/2026/v20i9523]

The Rotavirus A prevalence was 2.5%. The pathogen with the highest prevalence was Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) (52.6%, 20/38), Shigella/Enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (Shigella/EIEC (76.3%, 29/38), Norovirus (26.3%, 10/38) and Giardia was the main parasite identified. [10.1371/journal.pone.0356904]

Infant mice given a minimum dose of the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, comparable to those in adults. In contrast, infant mice receiving VLPs alone had substantially weaker immune responses. [10.1016/j.mucimm.2026.100401]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
诺如病毒感染的总体患病率为44%,其中GII型(73%)占主导地位,GI型占18%。9%的病例检测到GI/GII共感染。年龄与诺如病毒基因型分布存在显著关联(p=0.03),且GII型在≤5岁儿童中更为普遍。
与 DMSO 处理的对照相比,TAK-779 在感染后 48 小时和 96 小时 (hpi) 时,GII.17 HuNoV 复制分别增加了 2.3 倍和 6.0 倍。 [10.1111/gtc.70139]。
诺如病毒 在整个研究期间均被检测到,其中 3 月份的月度比例最高(34.4%)。高原州立专科医院阳性病例比例最大(68.9%),各机构差异有统计学意义。 [10.9734/sajrm/2026/v20i9523]。
轮状病毒 A 患病率 为 2.5%。患病率 最高的病原体是肠聚集性大肠杆菌 (EAEC) (52.6%,20/38)、志贺氏菌/肠侵袭性大肠杆菌 (Shigella/EIEC (76.3%,29/38)、诺如病毒 (26.3%,10/38),贾第鞭毛虫是鉴定的主要寄生虫。合并感染率较高(94.7%,36/38),大多数严重病例(75%,3/4)中存在细菌-病毒合并感染(73.3%,11/15)。

news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 诺如病毒 暴发 在荷兰布雷达的比利时营地,导致 175 名学生生病;荷兰时报报道。 [news-9f2eda30e3f3a6c1]
瑟西县学校因 诺如病毒 暴发 关闭,两名小学生的病毒检测呈阳性。关闭的原因是胃病 暴发,该学区在重新开放之前咨询了阿肯色州卫生部。 [news-dc0a1ef30374fbc1]
由于两例 诺如病毒 确诊病例,瑟西县学区于 2026 年 8 月 28 日星期五关闭。关闭是为了防止病毒传播的预防措施。 [news-ac66f3523cb83c34]
本文报告了 诺如病毒 诊断通过创新、背景需求和协作努力实现的转型。它被确认为对诊断进展及其对公共卫生影响的回顾。 [news-7404f2bf7974ec74]
诺如病毒 暴发 导致爱尔兰一家豪华酒店关闭。HSE 公共卫生部证实了对 暴发 的调查。 [news-318b025aab227bd9]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: Norovirus outbreak at a Belgian camp in Breda, Netherlands, resulting in 175 students falling ill; reported by NL Times. [news-9f2eda30e3f3a6c1]

Searcy County schools closed due to a norovirus outbreak, with two elementary school students testing positive for the virus. The closure was due to a stomach illness outbreak, and the district consulted with the Arkansas Department of Health before reopening. [news-dc0a1ef30374fbc1]

The Searcy County School District closed on Friday, August 28, 2026, due to two confirmed cases of norovirus. The closure was a precautionary measure to prevent the spread of the virus. [news-ac66f3523cb83c34]

The article reports on the transformation of norovirus diagnostics through innovation, contextual needs, and collaborative efforts. It is confirmed as a review of diagnostic advancements and their implications for public health. [news-7404f2bf7974ec74]
A norovirus outbreak caused a luxury hotel in Ireland to close. The HSE's Department of Public Health confirmed the investigation into the outbreak. [news-318b025aab227bd9]

papers.title: Enteric Pathogens in children under five with diarrhoea in a rotavirus vaccinated population in Coastal Ghana, 2023.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the introduction and wide coverage of vaccination regimes such as rotavirus vaccination globally, diarrhoea remains as a major public health problem with new studies showing an emerging pattern in its etiology. We assessed the etiology of diarrhoea in a population of children under five years appropriately vaccinated against rotavirus. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of children under five years reporting with diarrhoea at the district health facility in the Anloga district, Ghana. Stool samples of diarrhoea cases were tested for pathogens and co-infections using standard ELISA methods and TAQMAN Array Card RT-PCR Technology. The Vesikari Clinical Severity Scoring System was used to classify diarrhoea severity. Data generated was described descriptively. RESULTS: Median age was 21.5 (IQR:12,30)months, 55.3%(21/38) with being male. About half of the cases were moderate diarrhoea severity (20/38). The Rotavirus A prevalence was 2.5%. The pathogen with the highest prevalence was Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) (52.6%, 20/38), Shigella/ Enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (Shigella/EIEC (76.3%, 29/38), Norovirus (26.3%, 10/38) and Giardia was the main parasite identified. The rate of co-infection was high (94.7%, 36/38). Co-infections with bacteria-virus present had more moderate-severe diarrhoea cases (73.3%, 11/15). Norovirus was present in most of the severe cases (75%, 3/4). CONCLUSION: The leading diarrhoea pathogens found were EAEC, Shigella/EIEC and Norovirus. The rate of pathogen co-infection was very high with bacteria-virus related co-infections affecting diarrhoea severity. The study recommends periodic diarrhoea pathogen surveillance through Ghana Health Service collaborating with research institutions such as Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR). Also, enhancing water, sanitation and hygiene practices at the district, community and individual levels as a means of diarrhoea prevention in the absence of additional vaccines for other diarrhoea pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the etiology of diarrhoea in children under five years in a rotavirus vaccinated population in Coastal Ghana. The research aimed to identify the leading pathogens causing diarrhoea and assess the impact of co-infections. Stool samples were tested using ELISA and RT-PCR methods, revealing that Norovirus had a prevalence of 26.3%, while Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) and Shigella/EIEC were the most common pathogens. Co-infections were prevalent, with 94.7% of cases involving multiple pathogens, and these co-infections were associated with more severe diarrhoea. The findings highlight the need for targeted surveillance and improved hygiene practices to address diarrhoea in the absence of vaccines for other pathogens. The study's results are descriptive and do not provide detailed statistical analysis, which may limit the confidence in the conclusions.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:尽管全球已推广轮状病毒疫苗接种等疫苗接种方案并实现广泛覆盖,腹泻仍是一项主要的公共卫生问题,新研究显示其病因谱呈现新兴态势。我们评估了完成轮状病毒疫苗接种的5岁以下儿童腹泻病因谱。方法:在加纳安洛加区的区级卫生机构开展一项5岁以下儿童腹泻病例的横断面研究。采集腹泻病例粪便标本,使用标准ELISA方法和TAQMAN Array Card RT-PCR技术检测病原体及共感染。采用Vesikari临床严重程度评分系统对腹泻严重程度进行分类。对生成的数据进行描述性分析。结果:中位年龄为21.5个月(IQR:12,30),55.3%(21/38)为男性。约半数病例为中度腹泻严重程度(20/38)。轮状病毒A 患病率为2.5%。病原体中患病率最高的是肠集聚性大肠埃希菌(EAEC)(52.6%,20/38),其次为志贺菌/肠侵袭性大肠埃希菌(志贺菌/EIEC)(76.3%,29/38)、诺如病毒(26.3%,10/38),主要寄生虫为贾第虫。共感染率高(94.7%,36/38)。细菌-病毒共感染病例中,中度-重度腹泻病例占比更高(73.3%,11/15)。诺如病毒在大多数重度病例中检出(75%,3/4)。结论:主要腹泻病原体为EAEC、志贺菌/EIEC及诺如病毒。病原体共感染率极高,细菌-病毒相关共感染影响腹泻严重程度。研究建议通过加纳卫生服务与诺奎纪念医学研究所(NMIMR)等研究机构合作,定期开展腹泻病原体监测。同时,在缺乏其他腹泻病原体疫苗的情况下,通过加强区级、社区及个体层面的饮水、环境卫生与个人卫生实践,预防腹泻。

papers.title: Viral gastroenteritis: Molecular epidemiology of human norovirus by RT-PCR at University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of Congo
papers.abstract: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

INTRODUCTION Noroviruses (NoV) are non-enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Caliciviridae and are 2 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. recognized as the leading etiological agents of acute viral gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide (Winder et al., 2022). They are responsible for a substantial proportion of sporadic and epidemic gastroenteritis cases across all age groups and contribute significantly to morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals (Troeger et al., 2017). Due to their low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and high transmissibility, NoV infections represent a major global public health concern (World Health Organization (WHO), 2024; Patel et al., 2009). Diarrheal diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children under five years of age, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Recent estimates indicate that AGE accounts for hundreds of thousands of childhood deaths annually, with the highest disease burden occurring in Africa and South Asia (Sarno et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2017). Following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines, the epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis has changed considerably, with norovirus emerging as the predominant viral cause of AGE in many regions worldwide (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022). In sub-Saharan Africa, norovirus infections represent an increasing public health challenge. Several studies conducted in Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Gabon, and Cameroon have reported substantial prevalence rates among children presenting with acute diarrhea (Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Afework et al., 2022; Louya et al., 2019; Rönnelid et al., 2020; Tegegne et al., 2024). However, the true burden of norovirus infection in the region remains underestimated due to limited access to molecular diagnostic methods, inadequate laboratory infrastructure, weak surveillance systems, and underreporting of gastroenteritis cases. These challenges hinder accurate estimation of disease burden and the development of effective prevention and control strategies. In developing countries, poor sanitation, limited access to safe drinking water, overcrowding, and inadequate healthcare resources contribute substantially to the transmission of enteric viruses, including NoV (Rönnelid et al., 2020). In the Republic of Congo, only a limited number of studies have investigated the epidemiology of norovirus infections. A previous study conducted in Brazzaville reported a prevalence of approximately 27% among hospitalized children with acute diarrhea (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023). Nevertheless, available epidemiological data remain scarce and fragmented. In 2020, the Republic of the Congo experienced an increase in cases of acute diarrheal disease, particularly among children requiring hospital care. Globally, norovirus had already emerged as the leading viral cause of epidemic AGE following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs. However, despite this epidemiological context, molecular epidemiological data describing circulating norovirus genogroups were unavailable in the Republic of Congo. Therefore, documenting norovirus circulation during this period represented an important public health priority and provided baseline epidemiological information for the country (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). Ideally, effective surveillance systems supported by routine molecular diagnostic testing would enable continuous monitoring of circulating norovirus strains, early detection of outbreaks, and implementation of evidence-based public health interventions. However, in the Republic of the Congo, routine laboratory diagnosis of norovirus is not widely available, and epidemiological surveillance remains limited. Consequently, information regarding circulating geno- groups, transmission patterns, and associated risk factors remains insufficient. This lack of epidemiological information may have important public health implications, including delayed outbreak detection, inadequate allocation of healthcare resources, reduced effectiveness of preventive inter- ventions, and limited preparedness for future vaccine implementation programs. Strengthening local epidemio- logical evidence is therefore essential for improving disease control strategies and informing national health policies. Therefore, the present study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of norovirus among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. By addressing existing knowledge gaps, this study seeks to provide valuable epidemio- logical evidence to support norovirus surveillance, prevention, and control strategies in the Republic of Congo. MATERIALS AND METHODS Ethics statement This study was approved by the Health Sciences Research Ethics Committee of the Republic of the Congo (Reference No. 286/MRSIT/IRSSA/CERSSA). Written informed consent was *Corresponding author. E-mail: anicetboumba1974@gmail.com. Author(s) agree that this article remain permanently open access under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 International License obtained from the parents or legal guardians of all participating children before enrollment. Study population A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June 1 to November 1, 2020, in the Pediatric Emergency Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo. The study population consisted of children aged between 28 days and 17 years presenting with acute gastroenteritis during the study period, regardless of their immunological status. Acute gastroenteritis was defined as the passage of three or more loose or watery stools within a 24-h period. Children younger than 28 days of age, those presenting with bloody or mucoid diarrhea, and those with chronic or prolonged gastroenteritis were excluded from the study. The inclusion of a broad pediatric age range (28 days to 17 years) was intended to provide a comprehensive assessment of norovirus circulation across the pediatric population attending the referral hospital. Although norovirus infections are more frequently reported among children under five years of age, older children may also contribute to transmission dynamics and disease burden. Sample collection Participants were recruited using a consecutive sampling strategy. All eligible children presenting during the study period were enrolled consecutively until the target sample size was reached. The sample size of 50 participants corresponded to all eligible patients recruited during the study period and reflected the logistical and financial constraints associated with molecular testing. Although relatively small, this sample provided preliminary epidemiological data on norovirus infections among children with acute gastroenteritis in Brazzaville. A structured questionnaire was administered to collect sociodemographic, environmental, and clinical information. Stool samples were collected from all enrolled participants and transported under appropriate conditions to the laboratory. Samples were stored at −80°C until molecular analysis. Molecular analyses were performed at the Molecular Biology Laboratory of the Marie Madeleine GOMBES Foundation in Pointe-Noire. RNA extraction RNA extraction was performed using the Stool Total RNA Purification Kit Dx (NORGEN BIOTEK CORPORATION, Canada), following the manufacturer's instructions. This method is designed for isolation and purification of high-quality total RNA from stool samples, and based on spin column chromatography using Norgen’s proprietary resin as the separation matrix. RNA extracts were stored at -20°C prior to NoV detection and genogroup identification. Detection of NoV RNA and genotyping by real-time PCR Detection and genogroup identification of norovirus were performed using the RealStar Norovirus reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) Kit 3.0 (Altona Diagnostics, Germany). This assay allows qualitative detection and differentiation of norovirus genogroups GI and GII. The assay differentiates genogroups GI and GII using genotype-specific primers and hydrolysis probes labeled with distinct fluorescent dyes. Detection of fluorescence in the GI channel alone was interpreted as GI infection, whereas fluorescence detected only in the GII channel indicated GII infection. Simultaneous amplification in both channels, Amona et al. 3 together with valid internal and external controls, was interpreted as a mixed GI/GII infection according to the manufacturer's instructions. Positive and negative controls provided by the manufacturer were included in each RT-PCR run to ensure assay reliability. In addition, the heterologous internal control included in the kit was used to monitor both nucleic acid extraction efficiency and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) inhibition. Amplification was carried out on a MIC qPCR thermocycler using the following thermal profile: reverse transcription at 55°C for 20 min, initial denaturation at 95°C for 2 min, followed by 45 amplification cycles consisting of denaturation at 95°C for 15 s, annealing at 55°C for 45 s, and extension at 72°C for 15 s. All molecular procedures were conducted according to established laboratory quality assurance procedures, including standardized operating protocols, equipment maintenance, contamination prevention measures, and validation of control reactions before interpretation of results. Statistical analysis Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software version 27.0.1. Categorical variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test when appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Student’s t-test. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value < 0.05. RESULTS Socio-demographic and clinical characteristics of the study population A total of 50 children presenting with acute gastroenteritis were enrolled in this study. The majority of participants were aged ≤ 5 years (80%), while children older than 5 years represented 20% of the study population. The sex distribution was balanced, with 25 females (50%) and 25 males (50%). Regarding socioeconomic status, more than half of the participants originated from low-income households, while two-thirds were exposed to poor hygiene conditions, which is consistent with the continuing sanitation challenges reported in several low- income countries (Okesanya et al., 2024; WHO, 2025). Clinically, fever was observed in 80% of participants, increased stool frequency in 86%, and signs of dehydration were reported in all enrolled children (100%) (Table 1). Prevalence and distribution of NoV genogroups Norovirus RNA was detected in 22 of the 50 stool samples analyzed, resulting in an overall molecular prevalence of 44%. Among the positive samples, genogroup GII was the predominant circulating strain and was detected in 16 of 22 positive cases (73%). Genogroup GI was identified in 4 cases (18%), while mixed GI/GII infections were observed in 2 cases (9%), demonstrating the co-circulation of multiple norovirus 4 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. Table 1. Association between clinical manifestations and genogroups Analysis revealed a statistically significant association between age group and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03). Children aged ≤ 5 years were more frequently infected with genogroup GII compared with older children. No statistically significant association was observed between norovirus genogroups and clinical manifestations, including diarrhea, vomiting, fever, stool volume, or dehydration (p > 0.05) (Table 3). These findings suggest that although genogroup GII predominates among younger children, the clinical presentation of norovirus infection remains largely similar across circulating genogroups. DISCUSSION Acute gastroenteritis remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among children worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to healthcare, safe drinking water, and adequate sanitation remains limited. In recent years, norovirus has emerged as the leading viral cause of acute gastroenteritis following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). In the present study, the molecular prevalence of norovirus infection among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis was 44%. This prevalence is higher than that previously reported in the Republic of the Congo by Louya et al. (2019) and exceeds estimates reported from neighboring African countries, including Gabon, Ethiopia, and Nigeria (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023; Manouana et al., 2021; Tegegne et al., 2024; Omosigho et al., 2025). The relatively high prevalence observed in this study may be attributed to differences in study populations, healthcare- seeking behavior, seasonal variations, environmental conditions, and the use of sensitive molecular diagnostic techniques. Furthermore, the higher prevalence may be explained by the fact that sampling was conducted during the 2020 diarrheal disease epidemic, when viral gastroenteritis activity was particularly intense. analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses recognized as predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled, with eighty percent aged ≤5 years.
analysis.methods: Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of norovirus infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. A significant association was observed between age and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. The study identified GII as the dominant genogroup and highlighted age-related differences in genogroup distribution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures to improve prevention and control strategies for norovirus gastroenteritis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and small sample size limit causal inference and generalizability. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection bias and lack of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the molecular epidemiology of human norovirus among children with acute gastroenteritis (AGE) in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center, it enrolled 50 children aged 28 days to 17 years, with 80% aged ≤5 years. Using real-time RT-PCR, the overall norovirus prevalence was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%) and 9% exhibiting GI/GII co-infections. A significant age association was found (p = 0.03), with GII more prevalent in children ≤5 years. Clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). The study concludes norovirus is a key cause of pediatric AGE locally and recommends integrating molecular diagnostics into surveillance and improving sanitation. Limitations include the small sample size, cross-sectional design, and potential selection bias, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性胃肠炎 (AGE) 是非洲的一个主要公共卫生问题,急性胃肠炎 被认为是主要病毒病原。然而,刚果共和国,特别是布拉柴维尔,其流行病学影响仍然没有得到充分报告。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项描述性横断面研究于2020年6月至11月在布拉柴维尔大学医疗中心开展。共纳入50名年龄为28天至17岁且出现急性胃肠炎(AGE)症状的儿童,其中80%的患儿年龄≤5岁。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 分析粪便样本,以检测病毒 RNA 并区分 GI 和 GII 基因组。
elements_zh.main_results: 诺如病毒感染的总体患病率为44%,其中GII型(73%)占主导地位,GI型占18%。9%的病例检测到GI/GII共感染。年龄与诺如病毒基因型分布存在显著关联(p=0.03),且GII型在≤5岁儿童中更为普遍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 诺如病毒 是布拉柴维尔儿童 AGE 的一个重要原因。该研究将 GII 确定为主要基因组,并强调了基因组分布中与年龄相关的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持将分子诊断方法纳入国家诺如病毒监测计划,并加强卫生措施以改善诺如病毒胃肠炎的预防与控制策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的横断面设计和小样本量限制了因果推断和结果的普遍性。由于潜在的选择性偏倚和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.source_body_en: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

papers.title: Treatment With Ruxolitinib and TAK-779 Enhances GII.17 Human Norovirus Replication and Enables Serial Passaging in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
papers.abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

papers.source_body_en: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

papers.title: Zymosan-adjuvanted intranasal norovirus virus-like particle vaccine induces antiviral mucosal immune responses in infant mice.
papers.abstract: Infants require repeated immunizations of injectable-type vaccines against different pathogens because their immune systems are weaker than those of adults. However, these injectable vaccines cause physical and psychological discomfort. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop pain-free mucosal vaccines that are optimized for immunologically immature infants. Using an infant murine model, we examined the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant. The intranasal immunization of infant mice with VLPs alone induced mucosal and systemic VLP-specific immune responses that were substantially weaker than those of adults. In contrast, infant mice administered a minimum dose of intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, at levels comparable to those in adults. Importantly, intestinal and salivary antibodies elicited by intranasal immunization with the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine effectively inhibited norovirus propagation in human-induced pluripotent stem cellderived intestinal epithelial cells. These findings suggest that the intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine is an effective mucosal vaccine candidate for infants. It may help reduce the pain associated with injections and the number of immunizations infants required to achieve sufficient protective immunity against norovirus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of developing pain-free mucosal vaccines for infants, as their immune systems are less mature and injectable vaccines cause discomfort. There is an urgent need for vaccines optimized for immunologically immature infants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used an infant murine model to examine the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant. The vaccine was tested in infant mice to assess its ability to induce immune responses.
analysis.methods: The researchers administered the intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine to infant mice and compared the resulting immune responses to those induced by VLPs alone. They measured levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies and plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies.
analysis.main_results: Infant mice given a minimum dose of the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, comparable to those in adults. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine can effectively induce mucosal immune responses in infants, which is a novel approach for developing vaccines tailored to their immunological needs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the development of mucosal vaccines for infants, which could reduce the need for painful injections and improve the efficiency of achieving protective immunity against norovirus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an infant murine model, which may not fully represent human immune responses. However, the evidence is strong as it directly compares vaccine-induced immune responses in infants to those in adults using a well-defined experimental setup.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of a zymosan-adjuvanted intranasal norovirus virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine to induce mucosal immune responses in infant mice. The research was motivated by the need for pain-free vaccines for infants, as injectable vaccines are less effective and cause discomfort. Using an infant murine model, the study found that the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine significantly increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies and plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies in infant mice, comparable to those in adults. These findings suggest that the vaccine could be an effective mucosal vaccine candidate for infants, potentially reducing the need for multiple painful injections. The study's results are relevant for developing vaccines optimized for immunologically immature hosts, but its reliance on a murine model limits direct applicability to humans.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决为婴儿开发无痛粘膜 疫苗 的挑战,因为他们的免疫系统不太成熟,注射 疫苗 会引起不适。迫切需要针对免疫不成熟婴儿进行优化的 疫苗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用婴儿小鼠模型来检查鼻内 诺如病毒 病毒样颗粒 (VLP) 疫苗 与酵母聚糖作为佐剂的有效性。在婴儿小鼠中测试了 疫苗,以评估其诱导 免疫应答 的能力。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员向幼年小鼠鼻内注射含酵母聚糖佐剂的 VLP 疫苗,并将所得的 免疫应答 与单独 VLP 诱导的 免疫应答 进行比较。他们测量了肠道和唾液 VLP 特异性 IgA 抗体和血浆 VLP 特异性 IgG 抗体的水平。
elements_zh.main_results: 给予最低剂量的酵母聚糖佐剂的 VLP 疫苗 的婴儿小鼠表现出肠道和唾液 VLP 特异性 IgA 抗体以及血浆 VLP 特异性 IgG 抗体水平的增加,与成人相当。相比之下,仅接受 VLP 的幼年小鼠的 免疫应答 明显较弱。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,酵母聚糖佐剂的 诺如病毒 VLP 疫苗 可以有效诱导婴儿粘膜 免疫应答,这是一种针对婴儿免疫需求开发 疫苗 的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为婴儿粘膜疫苗的发育提供了重要的见解,这可以减少注射疼痛的需要,并提高实现针对诺如病毒的保护性免疫的效率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于婴儿小鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它使用明确的实验设置直接比较了婴儿中 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 与成人中的 疫苗。

papers.title_zh: 含酵母聚糖佐剂的鼻喷诺如病毒病毒样颗粒疫苗在婴幼鼠中诱导抗病毒药物黏膜免疫应答
papers.source_body_en: Infants require repeated immunizations of injectable-type vaccines against different pathogens because their immune systems are weaker than those of adults. However, these injectable vaccines cause physical and psychological discomfort. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop pain-free mucosal vaccines that are optimized for immunologically immature infants. Using an infant murine model, we examined the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant. The intranasal immunization of infant mice with VLPs alone induced mucosal and systemic VLP-specific immune responses that were substantially weaker than those of adults. In contrast, infant mice administered a minimum dose of intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, at levels comparable to those in adults. Importantly, intestinal and salivary antibodies elicited by intranasal immunization with the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine effectively inhibited norovirus propagation in human-induced pluripotent stem cellderived intestinal epithelial cells. These findings suggest that the intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine is an effective mucosal vaccine candidate for infants. It may help reduce the pain associated with injections and the number of immunizations infants required to achieve sufficient protective immunity against norovirus.

papers.title: Detection of Norovirus in Children 0-5 Years Presenting with Acute Diarrhoea in Three Selected Tertiary Health Facilities in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Norovirus is a global health concern and is considered a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis across all age groups, resulting in sporadic infections and epidemic or endemic outbreaks worldwide. Human norovirus infection accounts for substantial morbidity and mortality annually, particularly among children younger than 5 years. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of norovirus and the risk factors associated with infection among children presenting with acute diarrhoea in three selected tertiary health facilities in Jos. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among paediatric inpatients and general outpatient attendees from January to November 2020. Consenting participants were recruited using simple random sampling, and a stool sample was collected from each child. Data were analysed using STATA statistical software, version 15. Norovirus antigen was detected in 61 of 184 samples using the MyBioSource Norovirus Antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, giving an overall prevalence of 33.2%. Plateau State Specialist Hospital accounted for the largest proportion of positive cases (68.9%), and the difference by facility was statistically significant. Among positive cases, 62.3% were male and 37.7% were female, although sex was not significantly associated with infection. The highest proportion of infections occurred among children aged 7–12 months (32.8%). Norovirus was detected throughout the study period, with the highest monthly proportion recorded in March (34.4%). Body temperature was significantly associated with norovirus infection, with 45.9% of positive cases occurring among children with temperatures of 38.0–38.9°C. The observed prevalence highlights the need to strengthen norovirus prevention, surveillance, and control interventions in Jos and to support evidence-informed consideration of future vaccination strategies. It is recommended that children and parents practice hand hygiene by washing frequently with soap and water, properly disinfect contaminated surfaces using bleach-based cleaners, and thoroughly wash fruits and vegetables before consumption to reduce risk of norovirus infection.

papers.title_zh: 尼日利亚乔斯市高原州三家选定三级医疗机构中0-5岁儿童急性腹泻患者诺如病毒检测
papers.source_body_en: Norovirus is a global health concern and is considered a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis across all age groups, resulting in sporadic infections and epidemic or endemic outbreaks worldwide. Human norovirus infection accounts for substantial morbidity and mortality annually, particularly among children younger than 5 years. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of norovirus and the risk factors associated with infection among children presenting with acute diarrhoea in three selected tertiary health facilities in Jos. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among paediatric inpatients and general outpatient attendees from January to November 2020. Consenting participants were recruited using simple random sampling, and a stool sample was collected from each child. Data were analysed using STATA statistical software, version 15. Norovirus antigen was detected in 61 of 184 samples using the MyBioSource Norovirus Antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, giving an overall prevalence of 33.2%. Plateau State Specialist Hospital accounted for the largest proportion of positive cases (68.9%), and the difference by facility was statistically significant. Among positive cases, 62.3% were male and 37.7% were female, although sex was not significantly associated with infection. The highest proportion of infections occurred among children aged 7–12 months (32.8%). Norovirus was detected throughout the study period, with the highest monthly proportion recorded in March (34.4%). Body temperature was significantly associated with norovirus infection, with 45.9% of positive cases occurring among children with temperatures of 38.0–38.9°C. The observed prevalence highlights the need to strengthen norovirus prevention, surveillance, and control interventions in Jos and to support evidence-informed consideration of future vaccination strategies. It is recommended that children and parents practice hand hygiene by washing frequently with soap and water, properly disinfect contaminated surfaces using bleach-based cleaners, and thoroughly wash fruits and vegetables before consumption to reduce risk of norovirus infection.

papers.title: Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance in Cities with Sewered and Non-sewered Sanitation: Evidence from Kampala, Uganda
papers.abstract: Summary Background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) enables community-level monitoring of infectious diseases. Most progress has focused on sewer-based surveillance, yet nearly half of the global population relies on non-sewered sanitation. In non-sewered settings, urban drainage channels have been used for poliovirus environmental surveillance, but their potential for a multi-pathogen WES with spatially defined catchments, and comparability to sewer-based surveillance, remains under-explored. Methods: Ten drainage channel sampling points with delineated micro-catchments (0.95-3.83 km2 with 12,885-44,146 people) were selected within Kampala. A total of 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent samples were collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025. A multi-target panel was quantified by digital PCR, including enteric viruses (Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus), respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)), non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae (V. cholerae), and Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator. Findings: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Concentrations were generally lower in drainage than WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations across most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, although comparability varied by target and location. Both concentrations and PMMoV-normalized concentrations varied across sampling locations. Trends between campaigns varied by pathogen target and were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus (8-23% in drainage channels; 3-10% in WWTP influents), while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected. Interpretation: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, with spatial heterogeneity implying neighborhood-level differences in disease prevalence. Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring. Funding: Eawag Discretionary Funding

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) in non-sewered urban settings, specifically focusing on Kampala, Uganda. It evaluates the detection of enteric and respiratory viruses, including Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus, and SARS-CoV-2, in urban drainage channels and wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influents. The study collected 255 drainage channel and 54 WWTP influent samples during two campaigns in 2025. Using digital PCR, the researchers quantified a multi-target panel, including Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus, and PMMoV as a fecal indicator. The results showed consistent detection of enteric viruses and PMMoV across all sampling points, with lower concentrations in drainage channels compared to WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. cholerae. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations in most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, though this varied by location and target. The study highlights the potential of drainage-based WES to provide spatially resolved public health data in non-sewered areas, similar to sewer-based monitoring. However, the findings are limited by the variability in trends between campaigns and the lack of clear explanations for these variations. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations and the absence of detailed causal interpretations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 废水和环境 监测 (WES) 可实现社区级传染病监测。大多数进展都集中在基于下水道的 监测,但全球近一半的人口依赖无下水道的卫生设施。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在坎帕拉境内选择了 10 个具有划定微集水区的排水沟采样点(0.95-3.83 平方公里,12,885-44,146 人)。在 2025 年 3 月和 9 月至 10 月的两次活动中,共收集了 255 个排水渠道和 54 个废水 治疗 工厂 (WWTP) 进水样本。
elements_zh.methods: 通过数字 PCR 对多目标组进行定量,包括肠道病毒(诺如病毒 GI 和 GII、轮状病毒)、呼吸道病毒(SARS-CoV-2、甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV))、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌(霍乱弧菌)和作为粪便指标的胡椒轻度斑驳病毒 (PMMoV)。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有排水渠道和污水处理厂进水中均检测到肠道病毒、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。除非 O1/O139 V 外,排水中的浓度通常低于污水处理厂进水。当通过 PMMoV 标准化时,大多数排水渠道的浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,尽管可比性因目标和位置而异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 大多数微小流域中,烟草花叶病毒(PMMoV)标准化浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,空间异质性表明疾病患病率在社区层面存在差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 流域划定的排水系统监测有潜力在无下水道环境中提供与基于污水的废水监测相当的空间分辨率公共卫生信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 不同监测周期间的趋势因病原体靶标而异,且未能通过任何单一微小流域特征得到解释。由于结果的可变性及观察趋势缺乏详细解释,证据强度为中等。

papers.title_zh: 有下水道和无下水道卫生设施的城市中的废水和环境 监测:来自乌干达坎帕拉的证据
papers.source_body_en: Summary Background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) enables community-level monitoring of infectious diseases. Most progress has focused on sewer-based surveillance, yet nearly half of the global population relies on non-sewered sanitation. In non-sewered settings, urban drainage channels have been used for poliovirus environmental surveillance, but their potential for a multi-pathogen WES with spatially defined catchments, and comparability to sewer-based surveillance, remains under-explored. Methods: Ten drainage channel sampling points with delineated micro-catchments (0.95-3.83 km2 with 12,885-44,146 people) were selected within Kampala. A total of 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent samples were collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025. A multi-target panel was quantified by digital PCR, including enteric viruses (Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus), respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)), non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae (V. cholerae), and Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator. Findings: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Concentrations were generally lower in drainage than WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations across most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, although comparability varied by target and location. Both concentrations and PMMoV-normalized concentrations varied across sampling locations. Trends between campaigns varied by pathogen target and were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus (8-23% in drainage channels; 3-10% in WWTP influents), while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected. Interpretation: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, with spatial heterogeneity implying neighborhood-level differences in disease prevalence. Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring. Funding: Eawag Discretionary Funding
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景:废水和环境 监测 (WES) 能够实现社区级传染病监测。大多数进展都集中在基于下水道的 监测,但全球近一半的人口依赖无下水道的卫生设施。在无下水道环境中,城市排水渠道已用于脊髓灰质炎病毒环境 监测,但其在空间限定集水区的多病原体 WES 中的潜力以及与基于下水道的 监测 的可比性仍有待探索。方法:在坎帕拉境内选择了10个划定微流域的排水沟采样点(0.95-3.83平方公里,12,885-44,146人)。在 2025 年 3 月和 9 月至 10 月的两次活动中,共收集了 255 个排水沟和 54 个废水 治疗 工厂 (WWTP) 进水样本。通过数字 PCR 量化了多目标组,包括肠道病毒(诺如病毒 GI 和 GII、轮状病毒)、呼吸道病毒(SARS-CoV-2、甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒) (RSV))、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌 (V. cholerae) 和胡椒轻度斑驳病毒 (PMMoV) 作为粪便指标。研究结果:在所有排水渠道和污水处理厂进水中一致检测到肠道病毒、非 O1/O139 霍乱弧菌和 PMMoV。除非 O1/O139 V 外,排水中的浓度通常低于污水处理厂进水。当通过 PMMoV 标准化时,大多数排水渠道的浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,尽管可比性因目标和位置而异。不同采样地点的浓度和 PMMoV 标准化浓度均有所不同。运动之间的趋势因病原体目标而异,并且不能用任何单一的微流域特征来解释。甲型流感病毒是最常检测到的呼吸道病毒(排水道中为 8-23%;污水处理厂进水中为 3-10%),而 SARS-CoV-2、乙型流感和 RSV 则很少检测到。解释:大多数微流域的 PMMoV 标准化浓度与污水处理厂进水相当,空间异质性意味着疾病 患病率 的邻里水平差异。流域划定的排水 监测 有潜力在无下水道环境中提供空间解析的公共卫生信息,与基于下水道的废水监测相当。资金来源:Eawag 任意资金

papers.title: Microbial assessment of recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter in patient room environment in a burn unit.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have demonstrated that environmental contamination with several epidemiologically important pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp, Acinetobacter, norovirus, and Clostridioides difficile, can persist for several days to months and contributes to the transmission of these pathogens. METHODS: This study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to determine the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. After disinfection, samples were taken from 6 environmental sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours. RESULTS: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was as follows: chair, 3 hours; overbed table, 2 hours; stock cabinet, 3 hours; and IV pump, 2 hours. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection and underscored the need for enhanced environmental cleaning, including continuous disinfection methods, to prevent transmission of health care-associated pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Healthcare-associated transmission of pathogens is influenced by environmental persistence and recontamination, yet the rapidity of recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection in high-risk units remains insufficiently characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective environmental sampling study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to quantify the time to recontamination of surfaces with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after terminal disinfection.
analysis.methods: Six high-touch environmental sites were sampled using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours following standard disinfection procedures.
analysis.main_results: Recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly: overbed table and IV pump at 2 hours, and chair and stock cabinet at 3 hours.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that recontamination occurs within hours after cleaning, highlighting the inadequacy of conventional disinfection and the need for continuous or enhanced environmental cleaning strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the implementation of continuous disinfection methods in burn units to reduce healthcare-associated transmission of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a single burn unit, a short observation window, and did not assess transmission to patients, warranting cautious interpretation and larger-scale validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the rapidity of environmental recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a burn intensive care unit after disinfection. Six high-touch surfaces were sampled hourly for 10 hours using Rodac plates. Recontamination occurred within 2–3 hours on all sampled sites, demonstrating that surfaces become recontaminated quickly even after cleaning. The authors interpreted these results as evidence that conventional disinfection is insufficient and that continuous or enhanced environmental cleaning is necessary to prevent transmission. The findings imply that burn units should adopt continuous disinfection strategies to reduce healthcare-associated Acinetobacter transmission. However, the study’s single-centre design, short follow-up, and lack of patient outcome data limit generalisability and strength of evidence.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have demonstrated that environmental contamination with several epidemiologically important pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp, Acinetobacter, norovirus, and Clostridioides difficile, can persist for several days to months and contributes to the transmission of these pathogens. METHODS: This study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to determine the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. After disinfection, samples were taken from 6 environmental sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours. RESULTS: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was as follows: chair, 3 hours; overbed table, 2 hours; stock cabinet, 3 hours; and IV pump, 2 hours. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection and underscored the need for enhanced environmental cleaning, including continuous disinfection methods, to prevent transmission of health care-associated pathogens.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 与医疗保健相关的病原体 传播 受到环境持久性和再污染的影响,但高风险单位消毒后多重耐药鲍曼不动杆菌再污染的速度仍不充分。

papers.title: Detection Patterns and Temporal Dynamics of Multiple Pathogens in Wastewater Using a TaqMan Array Card
papers.abstract: Background: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) complements clinical surveillance by capturing community-level circulation of infectious diseases, including asymptomatic infections.However, most multipathogen WBS studies have focused on pathogen detection and detection frequency, with limited evaluation of temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Objectives: This study aimed to characterize multipathogen detection patterns in wastewater using a customdesigned TaqMan Array Card (TAC) and explore temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Methods: Weekly influent samples (500 mL) were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025 (64 total samples).The TAC targeted 31 pathogen analysis groups encompassing respiratory, enteric, and selected high-concern pathogens, along with seven antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).Pathogen occurrence was evaluated based on week-based detection status and detection frequency, while Ct values were interpreted as a semi-quantitative indicator for exploratory assessment of temporal changes.Samples failing the predefined quality control criteria were re-extracted and reanalyzed, and all samples were ultimately included in the final analysis.Results: Ten pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, norovirus, adenovirus type F, and human rhinovirus, were detected in 100% of the study weeks.Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) showed increased detection during winter, with influenza A/H3 and RSV type B predominating among their respective subtypes.Semi-quantitative Ct values showed no consistent increasing or decreasing trend for SARS-CoV-2, but they declined during winter for norovirus and influenza A. In contrast, RSV showed increased winter detection without a corresponding decrease in Ct values.bla_KPC, bla_NDM, and vanA/B/ C were detected in all study weeks, and mecA and bla_OXA also showed high detection frequencies.Conclusions: TAC-based WBS enabled simultaneous characterization of multipathogen detection patterns, antimicrobial resistance gene detection, and exploratory assessment of temporal changes using semiquantitative Ct values.These findings support TAC-based WBS as an integrated tool for community-level infectious disease surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) complements clinical surveillance by capturing community-level circulation of infectious diseases, including asymptomatic infections. However, most multipathogen WBS studies have focused on pathogen detection and detection frequency, with limited evaluation of temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Weekly influent samples (500 mL) were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025 (64 total samples). The TAC targeted 31 pathogen analysis groups encompassing respiratory, enteric, and selected high-concern pathogens, along with seven antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).
analysis.methods: Pathogen occurrence was evaluated based on week-based detection status and detection frequency, while Ct values were interpreted as a semi-quantitative indicator for exploratory assessment of temporal changes. Samples failing the predefined quality control criteria were re-extracted and reanalyzed, and all samples were ultimately included in the final analysis.
analysis.main_results: Ten pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, norovirus, adenovirus type F, and human rhinovirus, were detected in 100% of the study weeks. Semi-quantitative Ct values showed no consistent increasing or decreasing trend for SARS-CoV-2, but they declined during winter for norovirus and influenza A.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that norovirus detection patterns in wastewater can be characterized using a TaqMan Array Card, and that semi-quantitative Ct values can provide insights into temporal changes in viral load.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of TAC-based WBS as an integrated tool for community-level infectious disease surveillance, particularly for tracking norovirus and other pathogens with seasonal variations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not include specific analysis of norovirus subtypes or genogroups, and the semi-quantitative nature of Ct values may limit the precision of temporal trend assessments. Confidence in the findings is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize multipathogen detection patterns in wastewater using a TaqMan Array Card (TAC) and explore temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values. Weekly influent samples were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025, targeting 31 pathogens and seven antimicrobial resistance genes. The results showed that norovirus was detected in all study weeks, with semi-quantitative Ct values declining during winter. The findings support TAC-based wastewater-based surveillance as a tool for community-level infectious disease monitoring, particularly for tracking norovirus and other pathogens with seasonal variations. However, the study's limitations include the lack of subtype-specific analysis and the potential imprecision of Ct values in assessing temporal trends, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基于废水的 监测 (WBS) 通过捕获包括无症状感染在内的传染病的社区级循环来补充临床 监测。然而,大多数多病原体 WBS 研究都集中在病原体检测和检测频率上,使用半定量 Ct 值对时间变化的评估有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年第 21~52 周,每周从天安和牙山的两个废水 治疗 工厂收集进水样品(500 mL)(总共 64 个样品)。TAC 针对 31 个病原体分析组,包括呼吸道、肠道和选定的高度关注病原体,以及 7 个抗菌素耐药基因 (ARG)。
elements_zh.methods: 根据每周的检测状态和检测频率评估病原体的发生,而 Ct 值被解释为探索性评估时间变化的半定量指标。未达到预定质量控制标准的样品被重新提取并重新分析,所有样品最终均纳入最终分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究周内 100% 检测到 10 种病原体,包括 SARS-CoV-2、诺如病毒、F 型腺病毒和人鼻病毒。SARS-CoV-2 的半定量 Ct 值没有表现出一致的上升或下降趋势,但 诺如病毒 和甲型流感病毒的半定量 Ct 值在冬季下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,废水中的 诺如病毒 检测模式可以使用 TaqMan 阵列卡进行表征,并且半定量 Ct 值可以深入了解病毒载量的时间变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持使用基于 TAC 的 WBS 作为社区级传染病 监测 的综合工具,特别是用于跟踪 诺如病毒 和其他具有季节性变化的病原体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究不包括对 诺如病毒 亚型或基因组的具体分析,Ct 值的半定量性质可能会限制时间趋势评估的精度。由于这些限制,人们对研究结果的信心是中等的。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: Weekly influent samples (500 mL) were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025 (64 total samples). The TAC targeted 31 pathogen analysis groups encompassing respiratory, enteric, and selected high-concern pathogens, along with seven antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).
analysis_en.methods: Pathogen occurrence was evaluated based on week-based detection status and detection frequency, while Ct values were interpreted as a semi-quantitative indicator for exploratory assessment of temporal changes. Samples failing the predefined quality control criteria were re-extracted and reanalyzed, and all samples were ultimately included in the final analysis.
analysis_en.main_results: Ten pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, norovirus, adenovirus type F, and human rhinovirus, were detected in 100% of the study weeks. Semi-quantitative Ct values showed no consistent increasing or decreasing trend for SARS-CoV-2, but they declined during winter for norovirus and influenza A.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that norovirus detection patterns in wastewater can be characterized using a TaqMan Array Card, and that semi-quantitative Ct values can provide insights into temporal changes in viral load.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of TAC-based WBS as an integrated tool for community-level infectious disease surveillance, particularly for tracking norovirus and other pathogens with seasonal variations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not include specific analysis of norovirus subtypes or genogroups, and the semi-quantitative nature of Ct values may limit the precision of temporal trend assessments. Confidence in the findings is moderate due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: 使用TaqMan Array Card检测废水中多种病原体的检测模式及时间动态
papers.source_body_en: Background: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) complements clinical surveillance by capturing community-level circulation of infectious diseases, including asymptomatic infections.However, most multipathogen WBS studies have focused on pathogen detection and detection frequency, with limited evaluation of temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Objectives: This study aimed to characterize multipathogen detection patterns in wastewater using a customdesigned TaqMan Array Card (TAC) and explore temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Methods: Weekly influent samples (500 mL) were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025 (64 total samples).The TAC targeted 31 pathogen analysis groups encompassing respiratory, enteric, and selected high-concern pathogens, along with seven antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).Pathogen occurrence was evaluated based on week-based detection status and detection frequency, while Ct values were interpreted as a semi-quantitative indicator for exploratory assessment of temporal changes.Samples failing the predefined quality control criteria were re-extracted and reanalyzed, and all samples were ultimately included in the final analysis.Results: Ten pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, norovirus, adenovirus type F, and human rhinovirus, were detected in 100% of the study weeks.Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) showed increased detection during winter, with influenza A/H3 and RSV type B predominating among their respective subtypes.Semi-quantitative Ct values showed no consistent increasing or decreasing trend for SARS-CoV-2, but they declined during winter for norovirus and influenza A. In contrast, RSV showed increased winter detection without a corresponding decrease in Ct values.bla_KPC, bla_NDM, and vanA/B/ C were detected in all study weeks, and mecA and bla_OXA also showed high detection frequencies.Conclusions: TAC-based WBS enabled simultaneous characterization of multipathogen detection patterns, antimicrobial resistance gene detection, and exploratory assessment of temporal changes using semiquantitative Ct values.These findings support TAC-based WBS as an integrated tool for community-level infectious disease surveillance.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:基于废水的 监测 (WBS) 通过捕获包括无症状感染在内的传染病的社区级循环来补充临床 监测。然而,大多数多病原体 WBS 研究都集中在病原体检测和检测频率上,使用半定量 Ct 值对时间变化的评估有限。目标:本研究旨在使用定制设计的 TaqMan 阵列卡 (TAC) 来表征废水中多病原体检测模式并探索时间变化使用半定量 Ct 值。方法:2025 年第 21~52 周从天安和牙山的两个废水 治疗 工厂收集每周进水样品 (500 mL)(总共 64 个样品)。TAC 针对 31 个病原体分析组,包括呼吸道、肠道和选定的高度关注病原体,以及 7 个抗菌素耐药性基因 (ARG)。根据每周检测状态和检测情况评估病原体发生情况频率,而Ct值被解释为探索性评估时间变化的半定量指标。对未达到预定义质量控制标准的样本进行重新提取和重新分析,所有样本最终纳入最终分析。结果:研究周内100%检出SARS-CoV-2、诺如病毒、F型腺病毒和人鼻病毒等10种病原体。甲型流感病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒病毒 (RSV) 在冬季的检出率有所增加,其中 A/H3 型流感和 B 型 RSV 在其各自的亚型中占主导地位。SARS-CoV-2 的半定量 Ct 值没有表现出一致的上升或下降趋势,但 诺如病毒 和甲型流感病毒的半定量 Ct 值在冬季有所下降。相比之下,RSV 在冬季检出率有所增加,但 Ct 值没有相应下降。bla_KPC、bla_NDM 和 vanA/B/C 在所有研究周均被检测到,并且mecA 和 bla_OXA 也显示出较高的检测频率。结论:基于 TAC 的 WBS 能够同时表征多病原体检测模式、抗菌素耐药基因检测以及使用半定量 Ct 值对时间变化进行探索性评估。这些发现支持基于 TAC 的 WBS 作为社区级传染病 监测 的综合工具。

papers.title: Evolution, diversity and distribution of human Noroviruses:From single hosts to global patterns
papers.abstract: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis examines norovirus diversity and epidemiology to address critical gaps in understanding its evolution and public health impact. It synthesizes evidence showing norovirus as a major global cause of acute gastroenteritis, with over 10 genogroups and 50 genotypes, including the antigenically variable GII.4. The study integrates host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level. Key findings highlight the virus's extensive diversity as a barrier to therapeutic and vaccine development, with no licensed antivirals or vaccines currently available. The work interprets these patterns as evidence of ongoing antigenic drift and calls for improved surveillance and intervention strategies. Limitations include the reliance on literature synthesis and wastewater data, which may not fully capture host-specific dynamics or treatment outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.source_body_en: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

papers.title: Colorimetric-Catalytic-SERS Trimodal Immunochromatographic Assay for Multi-Scenario Monitoring of Gastrointestinal Infections.
papers.abstract: Direct pathogen detection in stool samples is the gold standard for diagnosing gastrointestinal infections, yet substantial technical challenges remain. Here, we report a versatile immunochromatographic assay (ICA) for simultaneous detection of both bacteria and virus, integrating a trimodal readout strategy combining magnetic enrichment with colorimetric, catalytic, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signals. We developed a self-assembled magnetic SERS nanozyme by electrostatically layer-by-layer depositing multilayer PtIr nanoparticles and Au nanostars onto a magnetic core, affording strong peroxidase-like activity and electromagnetic enhancement. In addition, a multi-feature fusion neural-network model was designed for intelligent SERS signal analysis, enabling accurate quantification of pathogen concentrations. The method exhibits high analytical performance across all three modalities: in colorimetric mode, the visual limits of detection (vLODs) were 5 × 103 CFU/mL for Escherichia coli O157 and 0.05 ng/mL for norovirus; in catalytic mode, a 2 min substrate-catalysis step reduced the colorimetric vLOD by 100-fold; in SERS mode, the detection limits were further lowered to 8 CFU/mL and 0.11 pg/mL via a quantitative algorithm. Application to 116 clinical stool samples showed detection rates consistent with quantitative real-time PCR, while reducing the assay time to 1/8. Therefore, this trimodal ICA holds strong potential for rapid and accurate detection of gastrointestinal infections across diverse scenarios.

papers.title: Simplified Linear Dose‐Response Models for Low‐Dose QMRAs
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study analyzes widely used dose‐response (DR) models from potable reuse quantitative microbial risk assessments (QMRAs) to identify the low‐dose ranges where the log 10 ‐transformed probability of infection and pathogen dose exhibit a linear relationship. Target pathogens include norovirus, adenovirus, enterovirus, Cryptosporidium , and Giardia . This study (i) defines the low‐dose linear range for each DR model, (ii) extracts slope and intercept parameters via regression, and (iii) shows that municipal drinking water risk thresholds fall within these ranges. This promotes low‐dose risk estimation transparency, reproducibility, and accessibility for utility decision making, regardless of the underlying complexity of the DR model. Also, this study shows that within the low‐dose ranges relevant to potable reuse, commonly used DR models exhibit linear relationships with a slope of ~1. Therefore, each 10‐fold reduction in pathogen concentration, equivalent to one log reduction value (LRV), reduces risk by a corresponding order of magnitude. Finally, the outputs from the various DR models are separated by relatively constant risk differentials, thereby reducing the need for complex DR‐based sensitivity analyses when conducting potable reuse QMRAs.

The research focuses on human noroviruses, including Norovirus GI and GII, and their relevance to water safety. The study defines the low-dose linear range for each DR model, extracts slope and intercept parameters via regression, and demonstrates that municipal drinking water risk thresholds fall within these ranges. It finds that within these low-dose ranges, commonly used DR models exhibit linear relationships with a slope of ~1, meaning each 10-fold reduction in pathogen concentration reduces risk by an order of magnitude. The results suggest that the outputs from different DR models differ by relatively constant risk values, reducing the need for complex sensitivity analyses. The study's findings promote transparency and reproducibility in low-dose risk estimation for utility decision-making. However, the study does not provide detailed limitations or evidence strength assessments.
